answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale.. This works because the originality bar tightens as more low-quality answers appear, raising the per-alias cost of a coordinated fake campaign. Consider a sable as the anchor of the cost. A cedar stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a falcon...
